speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Can you describe the severity of the bleeding from your wisdom tooth extraction and how long it has persisted? Also, have you noticed any other unusual bleeding, such as frequent nosebleeds or heavy menstrual periods, in the past?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient was brought in by his mother for persistent bleeding following elective removal of wisdom teeth. The bleeding from the surrounding gums was minimally responsive to multiple gauze packs. The patient also has a history of easy bruising. Family history includes the patient's uncle who had similar issues with bleeding and a history of easy bruising and joint swelling.

speaker: Doctor
text: Does the patient experience prolonged bleeding after minor cuts, and does he have a history of hemarthrosis, which is bleeding into the joints? I will also check for any physical signs of joint deformity or swelling. REQUEST TEST: Coagulation Profile

speaker: Doctor
text: The prolonged partial thromboplastin time with a normal platelet count and bleeding time suggests a factor deficiency, likely hemophilia, given the family history. To distinguish between Hemophilia A and B, I need to check the specific clotting factor levels. REQUEST TEST: Factor VIII and Factor IX Levels

speaker: Doctor
text: Since Factor VIII and IX are normal, the prolonged PTT likely points to Hemophilia C (Factor XI deficiency), especially given the family history. REQUEST TEST: Factor XI Level

speaker: Doctor
text: The low Factor XI level confirms the diagnosis of Hemophilia C. DIAGNOSIS READY: Hemophilia C
